root_cause_criterion.variable: the direct invalid-character path's immediate no-value return from consumeBracedCodePoint(bool)
root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: return immediately after error(SMLoc::getFromPointer(curCharPtr_), "invalid character in unicode codepoint escape") forces EOF
root_cause_criterion.criterion: On the invalid-character path in consumeBracedCodePoint(bool), once error(...) forces EOF, control must return the function's no-value result immediately instead of falling through to failed = true; continue; and letting the loop post-increment run.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original records branch_returns_none=0 at the invalid-character handling site even though forceEOF has already moved curCharPtr_ to bufferEnd_. The fixed original executes the same source event with branch_returns_none=1, restoring the missing immediate-return obligation before the loop can re-enter.

nodes.state: At the last loop-condition read on the crashing path, curCharPtr_ is already greater than bufferEnd_, so evaluating *curCharPtr_ != '}' is the AddressSanitizer-reported out-of-bounds read.
Immediately after the first invalid-character error call returns on the crashing path, forceEOF has already positioned curCharPtr_ exactly at bufferEnd_.

edges.relation: Because the vulnerable invalid-character arm ignores the forced-EOF return path, the for-loop post-increment executes before the next condition read and advances the same curCharPtr_ value from bufferEnd_ to the later out-of-bounds condition-read cursor.
